observation.description: guide/getting-started/the-authoring-loop.md still tells a consumer that `@expo/snapback-vite`, the current React starter, the versioned-seed integration, and the Linux run 'still need one newly versioned public closure before this page can call the React command a public-registry path', and leads with the historical `@ccheever/snapback-*` alias story for '0.1.x'. This G1 arm proved the entire React path — scaffold, generate, typecheck, vite build, dev lifecycle, live acceptance, teardown — from the public `@expo/snapback-*` 0.1.7 closure. The page's hedge is now false and steers external consumers away from a working paved path; the alias paragraph invites installing the wrong scope.

competitorOutcome.description: Competitor getting-started pages document exactly the install command that works against their public registry state; none hedge their primary quickstart behind a future publication.

mustNotRegress: The guide's honesty discipline of never claiming a public-registry path before a verified closure exists — the fix is to update the claim now that the evidence exists, not to loosen the discipline.
smallestCoherentFix: Refresh the-authoring-loop.md: state that the 0.1.7 `@expo/snapback-*` closure is the public-registry React path (citing the publication ledger and this G1 capsule), and demote the `@ccheever` alias history to a clearly-labeled lineage note.
acceptanceWitness: The page's claims match a rerun of the G1 external smoke against the pinned closure version it names; guide freshness review (reviewed/reviewed-commit) updated in the same change.
